extracted.intended_audience: journalists, policymakers, researchers, and general readers interested in TikTok, platform regulation, and digital-safety controversies
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, legal requirements, and evaluative criteria used to judge TikTok's data practices, content moderation, security, and compliance across multiple jurisdictions. Includes specific statutory/regulatory frameworks, company technical/organizational measures (e.g., Project Texas/Project Clover), and public-safety / child-protection features described on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPPA compliance (children's online privacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting information from minors under the age of 13 is prohibited without parental consent; violations resulted in an FTC consent decree and fines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC reached a consent decree with ByteDance and fined it US$5.7 million for collecting information from minors under 13; as a response the company added a kids-only mode blocking uploads, profile-building, direct messaging, and commenting for kids. Later class-action settlements and ongoing FTC investigations relate to COPPA enforcement (e.g., March 2022 settlement for US$1.1 million; continued FTC scrutiny reported in 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: GDPR compliance and protection of minors' data (EU Data Protection Commission enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of children's personal data and transfers of personal data to China must comply with GDPR; breaches can trigger large fines and investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ireland's DPC launched investigations into TikTok regarding protection of minors' data and data transfers to China; the DPC fined TikTok €345 million in September 2023 for mishandling children data and over €500 million in April 2025 for illegally sending European user data to China. The DPC has opened further investigations (e.g., July 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-transfer limitations, localization, and third-party oversight (Project Texas / Project Clover)
rubrics_metrics.description: User data for a region should be stored and managed locally under oversight by an independent third party or government (e.g., USDS/Oracle oversight for US data; Project Clover for Europe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Texas creates TikTok US Data Security Inc. (USDS) to manage US user data, code, back-end systems, and moderation under CFIUS oversight, with Oracle reviewing data flows, digitally signing code, approving updates, and overseeing moderation. Project Clover discusses local storage in Ireland/Norway and third-party oversight of cybersecurity policies, data flows, and personnel access independently of TikTok.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security / foreign access concerns and CFIUS oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether foreign access or foreign-entity control of platform data or systems poses a national security risk and whether CFIUS or equivalent bodies are satisfied with mitigation (divestiture, joint-venture, or oversight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of American user content stored in China and ByteDance employees' access are central concerns; TikTok negotiated with CFIUS and designed Project Texas/USDS to report to CFIUS. Legislative actions (e.g., U.S. laws requiring divestiture, bans on government devices) and executive orders have been used to address these concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic transparency, recommendation risks, and DSA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the recommendation algorithm's risks for elections, mental health, and protection of minors and whether the platform complies with Digital Services Act (DSA) obligations including advertising transparency and algorithmic information requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European Commission investigations under the DSA examined algorithmic risks, requested additional information about algorithms, and in May 2025 found TikTok had violated digital advertising rules. The Commission opened probes into content aiming at children and advertising transparency (Feb–Dec 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-moderation policy clarity and enforcement (hate speech, praise of terrorism, political content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies must define prohibited content (e.g., praising terrorist organizations, hate speech, disinformation) and enforce removals consistently; transparency about takedowns and moderation practices is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikTok removed >775,000 videos and 14,000 livestreams praising Hamas; the platform has been accused of suppressing pro-Palestinian content and of censoring criticism of public figures (e.g., alleged censorship of Trump-critical content and 'Epstein' mentions). The page notes both internal moderation decisions and regional differences in what content is shown (algorithm hiding based on region).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and sponsorship transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform must follow digital advertising rules and disclose advertising practices and sponsorships to meet legal and policy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The European Commission found TikTok violated digital advertising rules under the DSA (May 2025). The page also documents sponsorships/partnerships (e.g., Olympics, Team GB, Wrexham), indicating need for transparent commercial disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of software code and vulnerability management
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform should maintain secure code, promptly patch vulnerabilities, and avoid shipping code that could be used to exfiltrate data (e.g., SMS spoofing, keylogger-like code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Check Point Research found an SMS spoofing vulnerability (January 2020) that was later patched; Felix Krause found in-app browser code with keylogger-like functionality (August 2022) which TikTok said was disabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal access controls, employee monitoring and misuse prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit, log, and audit employee access to user data; investigate and discipline misuse (e.g., accessing journalists' data) to prevent surveillance and improper internal investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: December 2022 confirmation that ByteDance employees in China and the US accessed two journalists' data to find leak sources; ByteDance fired four employees and the incident prompted DOJ and FBI investigations and Congressional inquiries. The page also recounts allegations of employees emailing US user data to China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child-safety product features and defaults (screen time, notifications, age-limited features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide age-appropriate defaults and controls (e.g., screen-time limits, notification curfews, default limits for under-18s) to reduce harm and comply with child-protection obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikTok added an addiction-reduction feature (break every 90 minutes), notification curfews (no push notifications after 9pm for 13–15 and after 10pm for 16–17), default screen time limits for under-18s (announced March 2023), and dashboards showing usage. These features responded to concerns about mental health and attention spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating algorithmic 'rabbit holes' and harmful content amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Take steps to prevent the recommendation system from amplifying content that promotes self-harm, eating disorders, suicide, or other harmful behaviors and ensure users receive prompts/resources when searching such topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2021, accounts engaging with content related to suicide/self-harm or eating disorders were shown more similar videos; TikTok said it is working to 'break up these rabbit holes' and the platform provides prompts offering mental-health resources for certain searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of sexual exploitation and effective moderation (livestream commerce and minors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent monetization or livestreaming mechanisms from enabling sexual exploitation of minors; promptly remove sexual content involving minors and cooperate with regulators when abuse is reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 2025 investigation in Kenya found TikTok profited from sexual livestreams involving minors; Kenya's Communications Authority ordered removal of sexual content involving minors and required a plan to strengthen moderation and child protection systems. TikTok takes a 70% cut of livestream earnings in that context, and moderators reported ineffective policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with investigations, subpoenas, and law-enforcement requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to subpoenas and cooperate with DOJ/FBI/regulatory investigations while protecting user privacy rights and following lawful process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia reportedly subpoenaed ByteDance regarding surveillance of journalists; the incident was investigated by DOJ/FBI and inquired about by the House Select Committee. Regulatory bodies (FTC, DPC, ICO, etc.) have launched probes requiring cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to national device-use bans and export/import restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure compliance with government device bans and national-level restrictions (e.g., banning the app on government devices or all users) and maintain operational continuity or lawful exceptions where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple governments and legislatures banned TikTok on government/staff devices (European Parliament, EU bodies, US federal and many states, US military branches). US federal law (No TikTok on Government Devices Act) and legislative proposals (H.R. 7521) have been used to restrict the app; enforcement and exceptions vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account eligibility and age/engagement thresholds for monetization/features
rubrics_metrics.description: Require minimum age and engagement metrics for eligibility to use creator monetization features or certain account types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of June 2024, requirements for certain features are: account holder at least 18 years old, 10,000 followers, and 100,000 views in the last month; eligible areas include several countries (Brazil, US, UK, France, Germany, Japan, South Korea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and evidence standards when asserting censorship or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of censorship or political bias should be corroborated with transparent evidence and explained by platform logs/technical issues where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accusations of censoring Trump-critical content and 'Epstein' mentions were met with TikTok's denial and blaming alleged power outages; observers noted algorithm/regional differences and the need for careful selection of hashtags/metrics when assessing moderation bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation and accountability (fines, settlements, and structural remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory noncompliance should trigger sanctions, remediation measures (product changes, monitoring), and, where necessary, structural remedies (divestiture, joint ventures, code oversight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include FTC fines and consent decrees, DPC fines, investigations under various regulators, and operational remedies such as Project Texas/USDS and the eventual joint venture with Oracle/Silver Lake to transfer operational control in response to US law requiring divestiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive partnership and cooperation with law enforcement and public safety agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with police and public authorities to remove content associated with criminal activity and support public-safety efforts while balancing privacy concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikTok worked with New Zealand and Australian police to delete accounts/videos associated with criminal gangs; the platform reported cooperation to counter violent and hateful organizations and received public praise from police leadership in that instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace practices and employee protections (labor standards, discrimination handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain reasonable working hours, address discrimination and retaliation complaints, and comply with labor and EEOC requirements to ensure a safe workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former employees alleged excessive workloads and retaliatory practices; two former ByteDance employees filed a complaint with the US EEOC in September 2023 alleging retaliation for discrimination complaints. Company statements emphasize support and flexibility but allegations indicate potential compliance issues.
